messages:
leo_t: Hi team - had a root canal with Midtown Dental on 2026-06-14 and they told me it's out-of-network. I paid $1,150 at the visit. My plan summary said root canals are covered at 60% OON but provider says they didn’t submit a prior predetermination so claim might be denied. Anyone navigated a dental predetermination/estimate process?

anna_peopleops: Sorry that happened @leo_t. Which dental plan are you on (DHMO/PPO/DPPO)? Some DPPO plans require a predet or pretreatment estimate for major work for full allowance.

leo_t: It's Redwood Dental DPPO. I tried to check the carrier site but the claim history shows nothing yet. Provider says they didn't submit because they thought I wanted to self-pay and would file for OON reimbursement.

maria_benefits: Ok quick steps: 1) Ask Midtown Dental to submit a predetermination/pretreatment estimate to the carrier (this asks the carrier what they allow before they pay). 2) If they won't, you can submit a member claim with itemized receipt + tooth codes (D3310 for root canal on molar, etc.) + pre-auth request. 3) Attach x-rays or clinical notes if carrier asks. Predetermination can convert an otherwise denied bill into an allowed benefit if submitted timely.

leo_t: Provider said they can retroactively submit a predet but some carriers deny retro predets if the service already occurred. Is that true?

maria_benefits: Some carriers treat predeterminations as advisory if submitted before service; after-the-fact submissions are considered claims. But it still helps: if the carrier agrees the procedure is covered, you may get reimbursement. Ask the provider to include a cover letter noting it was an urgent/infection-related RCT and include date of service and tooth number.

leo_t: Got it. If carrier denies, can Finance do a short-term reimbursement? I paid the clinic out of pocket.

finance_bot: [automated] Finance policy: We can issue a one-time out-of-pocket medical/dental advance if you upload the itemized invoice to Expensify with tag "dental-advance" and a short note explaining the status. Approval typically within 2 business days and will be reconciled if carrier reimburses.

leo_t: Thanks. Also how do I get the carrier to provide an EOB? They say it will post once claim is processed but if predet is submitted will that create a visible record?

maria_benefits: Predetermination requests sometimes show up under "predetermination/pretreatment" instead of claims in the portal. EOB is only generated after adjudication of a claim. If provider submits a claim, ask them to include patient member ID and our group number so it routes correctly. If claim is denied, the carrier will issue EOB with denial reason and next steps.

midtown_dental: [provider] We can file the predet today. Need full member ID (on the card) and tooth #30. We can also re-bill as a claim if you want. Patient signed a waiver at checkout saying they would pursue OON reimbursement.

leo_t: I'll DM a screenshot of my digital card to you @midtown_dental. Please submit predet and then claim if needed. If the carrier rejects because it was done prior to predet, we'll file appeal.

carrier_bot: [automated] Carrier guidance: For DPPO predetermination, submit the pretreatment estimate form with tooth codes and radiographs. Retroactive predeterminations are accepted for consideration but do not guarantee a different outcome than a standard claim. Typical predet response time: 10-15 business days. Appeals timeframe: up to 60 days. Link: https://carrier.example/dental-predetermination

maria_benefits: One more tip: if the provider can submit the claim with CDT/CPT codes and also include the predet in the notes, that helps claims review. If the amount is large, ask the provider to include clinical justification (infection, acute pain) to avoid a "not medically necessary" denial.

leo_t: Appreciate it. I'll DM the card and the receipt now and tag Expensify for the advance in case predet takes long. Will report back once provider submits predet or claim. :+1:
